- Overestimate prices after recent spikes, especially when sentiment is high (e.g., >0.8) — model tends to overshoot and fail to correct downward.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is low or negative (e.g., <0.4) — model misses downward momentum or fails to recognize bearish signals.
- Lag in correction: model often delays reacting to sentiment shifts — e.g., if sentiment drops from 0.8 to 0.2, price drop is forecasted later than actual.
- Mean reversion bias: model overweights recent highs and fails to anticipate pullback — especially in 30-day horizon when sentiment is neutral or declining.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts are prone to overconfidence in short-term momentum; sentiment decay should trigger earlier downward adjustments.
- High sentiment + recent price rise → model overestimates continuation; low sentiment + recent fall → model underestimates reversal.
